title: Profile of Singaporeans on Public Transport Concession Schemes
what_it_is: Profile of Singaporeans on Public Transport Concession Schemes

sections.label: Senior citizen concession scheme
sections.summary: The senior citizen concession scheme recognises seniors' contributions, with close to 900,000 residents aged 60 and above expected to qualify by 2020.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng) (for the Minister for Transport)
sentences.text: The concession scheme for senior citizens, which accounts for more than 40% of residents with concession cards, aims to recognise their contributions towards our nation.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng) (for the Minister for Transport)
sentences.text: By 2020, we expect that there will be close to 900,000 Singapore Residents aged 60 and above who will qualify.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng) (for the Minister for Transport)
sentences.text: Over the last five years, the average number of journeys made by senior citizens has increased by around 50% while the number of senior citizen concession pass holders rose by around 30%.

sections.label: Low-income public transport expenditure
sections.summary: Over the past decade, low-income residents' monthly public transport expenditure as a share of household income fell from 4.2% to 2.7%.

sentences.speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
sentences.text: Looking at the past decade, when we look at the low-income residents, the monthly expenditure on public transport as a proportion of their household income has come down from 4.2% to 2.7%.

sections.label: Concession funding and fare balance
sections.summary: Most concession schemes are cross-funded by full-fare paying commuters, and PTC must balance land transport financial sustainability with fare affordability.

sentences.speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
sentences.text: Except for the Workfare Transport Scheme and the persons with disabilities scheme, which are funded by the Government, the others are cross-funded by other full-fare paying commuters.

sentences.speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
sentences.text: So, there is cross-subsidy by other full-fare paying commuters.

sentences.speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
sentences.text: Ultimately, PTC has to take into consideration and to strike a balance between ensuring the financial sustainability of the land transport system and the fare affordability for our commuters.
